transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Um, hi. Well... my supervisor kind of told me I needed to come. I guess I keep leaving my station at work. Or, like, popping up during meetings when I'm supposed to stay put. He says it's becoming a safety problem... just because I take off before I even think about it. So... yeah. That's why.
Aside from these impulsive actions, do you find that you frequently struggle to stay focused on tasks or lose track of details when you are at work?

I mean... yeah, sometimes. Like if they make me do inventory logs, or... read the CNC training pages. I start out really trying, but after a few minutes, the numbers or words just kind of... blur together. I end up having to go back over it again because I didn't take any of it in. So... yeah, I guess.
Looking back at your time in school, did you struggle with these same issues—like difficulty focusing or acting without thinking—even back then?

Um... yeah. I guess. Even back in, like, elementary school... I was always getting notes sent home. I just couldn't really stay in my seat. I'd end up wandering around the room, or... talking over the teacher. Blurting stuff out. So... yeah, it's always been like that.
When you are trying to focus on those tasks, do you often make careless mistakes or lose things that you need to get your work done?
Um... no, not really. I don't think I lose things much. I just... I don't know, I haven't really noticed making mistakes like that.
When you are working on those tasks, do you often find that your mind wanders off and you lose your train of thought, even if you aren't necessarily making careless mistakes?
Um... I don't think so. I mean, I don't really notice my mind wandering off like that. I just... I get antsy, mostly. But I don't really lose my train of thought.
